scenes.title: Why does right use a minus sign?
body: Why is it f(x - 3), not f(x + 3)?
scenes.narration: Suppose f of x equals two x plus one, and you want to move its graph three units to the right. The confusing part is that the rule uses f of x minus three. That looks backward. Here’s the idea: a horizontal translation changes which input produces the same output; it does not change the line’s shape.

scenes.title: A translation moves points, not the slope
scenes.substitution: Same output 1 now occurs at x = 3
scenes.narration: Start with a point you know. Since f of zero equals one, the original line contains zero comma one. Moving right three units should send that point to three comma one. The slope must stay two because a translation slides the entire line without rotating or stretching it.

scenes.title: Why the inside sign is reversed
scenes.formula: g(x) = f(x - h) → right by h
scenes.substitution: x - 3 asks the old function for the input 3 units earlier
scenes.narration: Notice why the minus sign works. At the new x-value three, g asks the old function for f of zero. So the old output at x equals zero reappears three units later, at x equals three. This is where students often mix things up: outside the function, signs behave normally for up and down; inside the input, the sign is reversed for left and right.

scenes.title: Build and simplify the translated line
scenes.narration: Now substitute x minus three into the original formula. Two times x minus three plus one becomes two x minus six plus one, so g of x equals two x minus five. The intercept changed, but the slope is still two. That is exactly what we expect from a parallel shift.

scenes.title: Check the moved point
scenes.narration: Quick check: the original point zero comma one should become three comma one. And g of three equals six minus five, which is one, so the shift is correct. Recap the idea: horizontal translations change the input needed to get the same output, which is why moving right by h uses f of x minus h. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT.
